promptLatex: A circle has radius $10$, and a chord of the circle lies $5$ units from the centre. Tangents at the two ends of that chord meet at a point $T$. What is the distance from the centre of the circle to $T$, in units?
hintLatex: The line from the centre to the midpoint of the chord is also the line to $T$.
The radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent.
Right triangles $OMP$ and $OPT$ share the angle at $O$, so $OM \cdot OT = OP^{2} = 100$.
solutionLatex:
Let $O$ be the centre, $M$ the midpoint of the chord, and $P$ one of its endpoints. Since $OM$ is perpendicular to the chord, the centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of the chord. The tangents at $P$ and at the other endpoint are symmetric about that same line, so their intersection $T$ lies on line $OM$ as well, on the far side of $M$ from $O$.

At $P$ the radius $OP$ is perpendicular to the tangent $PT$, so triangle $OPT$ has a right angle at $P$. Triangle $OMP$ has a right angle at $M$, and the two triangles share the angle at $O$, since $OM$ and $OT$ lie on one line and $OP$ is common to both. They are therefore similar.

Matching corresponding sides gives $\frac{OM}{OP} = \frac{OP}{OT}$, so $OM \cdot OT = OP^{2} = 10^{2} = 100$. With $OM = 5$, that gives $OT = \frac{100}{5} = 20$.
